title: Enumerator configuration and time contracts
statement: Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, let $T_V$ be a time bound, and let $M_V$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine that decides $V$ within time $T_V$. Then there exist a natural number $b$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine $E$ such that for every Boolean input $x$ there are a family of configurations $\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ of $E$ on $x$, indexed by natural numbers, and a startup time satisfying the following conditions. Writing $w=C(|x|+1)^c$, the startup time is at most $b\bigl(T_V(|x|+w)+(|x|+w+1)^{c+1}\bigr)$, and $E$ reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(0)$ from its initial configuration within that startup time. The configuration $\mathrm{cfg}(2^w)$ is halted with output $[\mathrm{false}]$. For every $i<2^w$, there is a time at most $b\bigl(T_V(|x|+w)+(|x|+w+1)^{c+1}\bigr)$ such that, if $x$ concatenated with the width-$w$ little-endian binary word of $i$ belongs to $V$, the machine from $\mathrm{cfg}(i)$ halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$; otherwise it reaches $\mathrm{cfg}(i+1)$ at that time.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Boolean machine $M_V$ deciding $V$ within $T_V$
replaced:
Fix constants $C, c$, a language $V$ over the binary alphabet, and a machine $MV$
deciding $V$ within time $T_v$. Then there exist a constant $b$ and one finite
machine $E$ such that for every input $x$ --- writing $n = |x|$ and
$w = C(n+1)^c$ --- there is a rank-indexed family of configurations of $E$ on
$x$ with: $E$ reaches the rank-$0$ configuration from its initial configuration
within $b\,(T_v(n+w) + (n+w+1)^{c+1})$ steps; the rank-$2^w$ configuration is
halted with single-bit output false; and from each rank $i < 2^w$, within the
same budget, $E$ either halts with output true when $x$ concatenated with the
width-$w$ binary word of $i$ lies in $V$, or reaches the rank-$(i+1)$
configuration otherwise.
